target.title: fix(memory-wiki): bridge status crashes on malformed memory-plugin artifacts and ignores readMemoryArtifacts=false
target.body:
Closes #100899

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running memory-wiki in bridge mode with a memory plugin that exports malformed public artifacts would get `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'localeCompare')` from `wiki status` and the `wiki_status` agent tool — and where setting `bridge.readMemoryArtifacts: false` did not stop the agent-tool crash, because the status path never consulted that flag.

Concretely hit by `@mem0/openclaw-mem0` ≤ 1.0.14, which exports record-shaped artifacts with none of the file-backed fields (plugin-side report: mem0ai/mem0#6113, plugin-side fix: mem0ai/mem0#6114). But any plugin can misbehave; the gateway shouldn't crash on bad plugin data.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two small changes:

- `listActiveMemoryPublicArtifacts` now validates plugin-returned artifacts before sorting and drops malformed entries (and non-array listings) with a single warning naming the offending plugin — the same treatment `agentIds` already received in 4644e0c1025. Dropping rather than failing means one bad entry can't take down status for everything else, and the warning makes the plugin bug visible instead of silent.
- `resolveMemoryWikiStatus` now gates artifact enumeration on `bridge.readMemoryArtifacts`, matching the sync path in `bridge.ts` and the CLI's gateway routing, which already honor it. With the flag off, the artifact count reports `null`, consistent with non-bridge modes.

## User Impact

Bridge mode with a misbehaving memory plugin degrades to a logged warning instead of crashing `wiki status` / `wiki_status`, and `readMemoryArtifacts: false` now actually disables artifact enumeration on the status path.

## Evidence

- Crash reproduced end-to-end on `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.6.11` in Docker with `@mem0/openclaw-mem0` 1.0.14 (open-source mode, Qdrant, two stored memories): `openclaw wiki status` and `openclaw gateway call wiki.status` both fail with the `localeCompare` error; with `readMemoryArtifacts: false` the gateway RPC still fails. Full repro in the linked issue. Note the repro needs at least two artifacts — with one, `toSorted` never invokes the comparator, which is easy to false-negative on.
- New regression tests use the plugin's exact malformed shape: `src/plugins/memory-state.test.ts` ("drops malformed public memory artifacts instead of crashing the sort", "ignores a non-array public artifact listing") and `extensions/memory-wiki/src/status.test.ts` ("skips artifact enumeration when readMemoryArtifacts is disabled"). All three fail without the fix.
- Local lanes (Windows): `pnpm test:extension memory-wiki` — the touched files pass (`memory-state.test.ts` 17/17, `status.test.ts` 10/10, both including the new tests). The lane's four failures are symlink/hardlink safety tests in `bridge.test.ts`/`okf.test.ts` that fail identically on a clean `main` checkout in this environment (Windows symlink permissions) — untouched by this PR. `pnpm test:contracts:plugins` — one failure (`session-attachments.contract.test.ts`), also identical on clean `main`. `node scripts/check-src-extension-import-boundary.mjs --json` — clean (`[]`). Repo lint (oxlint shards) passes.

---

AI-assisted. I've reviewed every change and validated the behavior end-to-end myself (Docker repro above).

target.title: fix(openai): respect api:"openai-completions" config in transport normalization (#99273)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users setting `api: "openai-completions"` at the provider or per-model level for `openai/*` models were silently ignored. The transport was always forced to `"openai-responses"`, causing every `openai/*` call to hang to idle timeout when the user explicitly configured completions mode.

Previous iterations of this PR only fixed the provider-level path. This iteration adds per-model detection — when `api: "openai-completions"` is set on a specific model row (e.g. `models.providers.openai.models: [{id: "gpt-5.5", api: "openai-completions"}]`), it is now also respected.

Fixes #99273.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two independently incorrect things were happening:

1. **`shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`** had a single-char logic bug (`!==` vs `===`) that forced explicit completions config to Responses.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport`** shared the same predicate with the transport callback, but models that reach the resolved-model path carry `api: "openai-completions"` as a catalog default — the resolved model's `api` field does not carry provenance. So per-model user config like `{id: "gpt-5.5", api: "openai-completions"}` was indistinguishable from the catalog default `"openai-completions"` after resolution.

The fix has four parts:

1. **`hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig()`** — New helper that checks BOTH `config.models.providers.openai.api` (provider-level) and `config.models.providers.openai.models[].api` (per-model level) to distinguish user intent from catalog defaults.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport()`** — Rewritten with its own catalog-normalization logic (checks owner provider + default baseUrl + default api), decoupled from `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`.

3. **`normalizeResolvedModel` callback** — Checks `hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig` before calling `normalizeOpenAITransport`. When the user explicitly configured completions at either level, returns the model unchanged.

4. **`normalizeTransport` callback** — Checks `hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig` before calling `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`. When the user explicitly configured completions, returns `undefined` (no override).

**Not modified**: Codex Responses transport hooks, auth profiles, usage tracking, live catalog fetching.

## User Impact

Users who explicitly configure `api: "openai-completions"` at the provider level OR on a specific model row now have their configuration respected. Default behavior for catalog OpenAI models (normalize to Responses) is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Production-code proof — all 3 config levels

Proof script imports the real `buildOpenAIProvider()` and exercises both `normalizeResolvedModel` and `normalizeTransport` callbacks against catalog-default, provider-level, and per-model config scenarios:

```
$ npx tsx scripts/proof-99273-completions-config.mjs

[PASS] resolved: catalog → Responses
[PASS] resolved: provider-level explicit completions  
[PASS] resolved: per-model explicit completions        ← THE FIX (was broken)
[PASS] transport: catalog → Responses
[PASS] transport: provider explicit → undefined
[PASS] transport: per-model explicit → undefined        ← THE FIX (was broken)

6/6 passed
```

### Data flow proof — per-model config survives normalization

```
User config:  {openai: {models: [{id: "gpt-5.5", api: "openai-completions"}]}}
  ↓ model.ts:747-757
  metadataOverrideModel.api = "openai-completions"      (per-model wins)
  resolvedModel.api = "openai-completions"
  ↓ normalizeResolvedModel callback
  hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig(config, "gpt-5.5")
    → openaiCfg.models.some(m => m.id === "gpt-5.5" && m.api === "openai-completions")
    → TRUE → return ctx.model unchanged ✅
```

### Test regression

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)

$ npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts --run
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  246 passed (246)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts
→ exit 0
```

### What was not tested

| Not tested | Why acceptable |
|------------|----------------|
| Real OpenAI endpoint E2E for each config level | The proof exercises the exact `normalizeResolvedModel` and `normalizeTransport` callback functions with their real production implementations — the same functions the gateway calls. Whether the API key works beyond this transport-normalization boundary is a separate concern from this predicate fix. |

## Root Cause

Two coupled problems in `extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts`:

1. **`shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`**: A single-character logic error (`!==` for `===`) at L462 caused the early-return guard to execute the opposite of its intended behavior. But fixing this alone broke the transport path's catalog normalization.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport`**: Shared the same predicate, creating a coupling where the resolved-model path's catalog normalization and the transport path's per-request override used the same boolean function. After model resolution, the resolved `api` field carries no provenance bit — a per-model `api: "openai-completions"` config and the catalog default `api: "openai-completions"` are identical strings. The only way to distinguish them is to inspect the raw config.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Claude Opus 4.8 (Anthropic). The author understands and takes responsibility for all code changes.

target.title: feat(android): in-chat model picker with favorites and recents
target.body:
Related: #100699

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android users could not switch models in chat at all: the app had no model picker anywhere — the model catalog was only visible as a read-only provider readiness overview in Settings. iOS/macOS users can switch the session model from the composer; Android had no equivalent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a model chip to the Android chat composer that opens a bottom-sheet picker fed by the existing gateway model catalog, with Pinned / Recent / Models sections: star to pin/unpin without closing the sheet, tap to select. Selection patches the session via `sessions.patch { key, model }` (the same wire contract iOS/macOS use); pins and recents (capped at 5) persist in the app's plain preferences, and a recent is recorded only after gateway acceptance. A selection mutex orders model patches ahead of sends so the first post-selection message can never leave on the previous model. Because `sessions.patch` requires `operator.admin`, fresh Android connects now request that scope — exact parity with iOS, which already requests admin for token/password connects; previously paired device tokens keep their granted scopes (existing stored-scope narrowing) and simply can't patch models until re-paired, mirroring how `operator.talk.secrets` rolled out.

**Security note (deliberate decision, please weigh in):** `sessions.patch` is classified `operator.admin` in the gateway method descriptors, so this PR adds `operator.admin` to Android's fresh-connect scope request. This is exact parity with iOS, which already requests admin for every token/password connect (`shouldRequestOperatorAdminScope` in `apps/ios/Sources/Model/NodeAppModel.swift`), and follows the same rollout pattern as `operator.talk.secrets`: previously paired device tokens keep their narrower granted scopes. The alternative — a narrower gateway permission for model-only session patches — is a protocol/security contract change beyond this client PR's boundary; if maintainers prefer that, it should be its own gateway-side follow-up, and this scope request can be revisited then.

## User Impact

Android users can now switch the session model from the chat composer, pin favorites, and reach recently used models first. On gateways where the operator connection lacks admin scope, selection fails with a visible chat error and no state is polluted.

## Evidence

- `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` focused suites green: `ChatModelPickerTest` (section ordering, provider-qualified ref derivation), `SecurePrefsTest` (favorites/recents persistence round-trip, dedupe/cap), `ChatControllerModelSelectionTest` (recent recorded only on RPC success, rejection surfaces error and records nothing, send-after-select ordering), `ConnectionManagerTest`/`GatewayBootstrapAuthTest` (fresh-connect scope set incl. `operator.admin`, stored-token narrowing unchanged).
- `:app:ktlintFormat` clean on changed files; `:app:ktlintCheck` failures are pre-existing in five untouched test files (called out for transparency).
- `corepack pnpm native:i18n:sync` run for the new picker strings.

target.title: fix(agents): emit diagnostic when sessions_yield parks without continuation evidence
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_yield` without a continuation source silently parks an interactive direct session — the turn completes with `yieldDetected: true` and zero payloads, so the user sees nothing and the bot appears hung. This adds a diagnostic payload when the yielded turn has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, async tools, or cron adds, so the user gets a visible message instead of a silent hang.

- **Problem**: `run.ts` always returns no payloads when `yieldDetected=true`, even when no continuation source exists. The incomplete-turn fallback is suppressed by the yield flag, so no visible output reaches the user.
- **Solution**: Extract a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` helper in `incomplete-turn.ts` (the continuation subset of `hasAttemptTerminalState` minus self-reference, plus `countActiveDescendantRuns`), then call it from `run.ts` to check for concrete continuation evidence before trusting a yield as terminal. When payloads are empty and `yieldDetected` has no continuation sources, emit a diagnostic text payload.
- **What changed**:
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts` — new exported `hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt, activeDescendantCount?)` + `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant, placed next to sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` — inline predicate replaced with shared helper call; triple-nested ternary uses shared constant
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — 4 new tests: 3 diagnostic-suppression (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) + 1 async-tool purity
- **What did NOT change**: Yield acceptance semantics, `hasAttemptTerminalState`, `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`, liveness state classification. No existing yield path is altered.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #100065
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a model calls `sessions_yield` before establishing any continuation (before spawning subagents, sending messages, starting async tools, or scheduling cron work), the runtime accepts the yield unconditionally. The turn records `yieldDetected: true` with no payloads, liveness becomes `"paused"`, and the session produces no visible output. From the user's perspective the bot simply stops responding — no error, no fallback, no diagnostic.

The yield tool's own contract says "Use **after** spawning subagents; results arrive as next message." A yield before spawning violates this contract, but the runtime has no guard. This fix adds a user-visible signal so the silent park is replaced with a diagnostic message.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: `sessions_yield` without continuation evidence no longer returns empty payloads silently. A diagnostic text is emitted.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22.19, fix/yield-no-continuation-diagnostic-100065 branch
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Live proof: shared hasYieldContinuationEvidence logic (7 scenarios)
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { hasYieldContinuationEvidence } from "./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts";

function shouldEmitDiagnostic(attempt) {
  const hasContinuation = attempt.yieldDetected && hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt);
  if (attempt.yieldDetected && !hasContinuation)
    return { diagnostic: true, text: "⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume." };
  return { diagnostic: false };
}

const cases = [
  ["bare yield, no continuation", { yieldDetected: true }],
  ["yield + accepted spawn", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [{ runId: "c", childSessionKey: "k" }] }],
  ["yield + committed delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["answer"] }],
  ["yield + whitespace delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["   "] }],
  ["yield + empty spawn array", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [] }],
  ["yield + async tool in flight", { yieldDetected: true, toolMetas: [{ asyncStarted: true }] }],
  ["yield + approval prompt", { yieldDetected: true, didSendDeterministicApprovalPrompt: true }],
];
for (const [name, att] of cases)
  console.log(`${shouldEmitDiagnostic(att).diagnostic ? "DIAGNOSTIC" : "SILENT    "} — ${name}`);
NODE

# 2. Regression test suite (121 tests)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
# Real gateway run: sessions_yield without continuation → diagnostic emitted
$ openclaw agent --agent main --json --message 'Call sessions_yield. Do NOT spawn subagents, do NOT send messages, do NOT do anything else. Only call sessions_yield.'

{
  "result": {
    "payloads": [
      {
        "text": "⚠ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume.",
        "mediaUrl": null
      }
    ],
    "meta": {
      "yielded": true,
      "livenessState": "paused",
      "stopReason": "end_turn",
      "toolSummary": {
        "calls": 1,
        "tools": ["sessions_yield"],
        "failures": 0
      },
      "replayInvalid": true
    }
  }
}

# 7 production logic scenarios (node --import tsx)
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
DIAGNOSTIC — bare yield, no continuation
SILENT     — yield + accepted spawn
SILENT     — yield + committed delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + whitespace delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + empty spawn array
SILENT     — yield + async tool in flight
SILENT     — yield + approval prompt

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run

 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  121 passed (121)
```

```console
# Active descendant check: countActiveDescendantRuns() smoke test
$ node --import tsx -e "import { countActiveDescendantRuns } from './src/agents/subagent-registry-read.ts'; console.log('empty key:', countActiveDescendantRuns(''), '(safe fallback)'); console.log('unknown key:', countActiveDescendantRuns('no-such'), '(safe fallback)'); console.log('All returned 0 without throwing ✅');"
```

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. All 121 yield/incomplete-turn tests pass — no regression. Four new tests cover: (a) bare yield with no continuation → diagnostic emitted, (b) whitespace-only delivery text → NOT counted as continuation, (c) empty spawn array → NOT counted as continuation, (d) three suppression scenarios (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) → diagnostic suppressed.
  2. The change is purely additive: when a yield has continuation evidence (spawns, delivery, async tools, cron, or active descendant runs), behavior is identical to before.
  3. When a yield has no continuation evidence, a diagnostic payload `"⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume."` is emitted instead of an empty payload array.
  4. Normalized helpers (`hasAcceptedSessionSpawn`, `hasCommittedMessagingToolDeliveryEvidence`) correctly reject whitespace-only delivery text and empty spawn arrays — preventing false continuation signals.
  5. `countActiveDescendantRuns()` is safely imported and returns 0 when no active descendants exist, preserving the diagnostic for bare yields while correctly skipping it when the session has in-flight child work.

- **What was not tested**: Live Telegram/Discord environment (no bot tokens available). The gateway run used a local ZTE provider (Qwen3-235B-A22B), not a Telegram/Discord channel. The core diagnostic path (yield without continuation → user-visible message) is proven identical across all channels since it runs at the embedded-runner layer.

## Root Cause

Three compounding gaps allow the silent park:

1. **`sessions-yield-tool.ts`** — No validation at the tool level. Accepts any yield regardless of continuation state.
2. **`incomplete-turn.ts:261`** — `yieldDetected` causes `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText` to return `null` immediately, suppressing the incomplete-turn fallback.
3. **`run.ts:4125-4148`** — The yield-specific path always returns no payloads, regardless of whether continuation evidence exists.

This PR addresses (3) only — it is the safest additive fix. A deeper fix for (1) would require a product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a model calls `sessions_yield` without establishing any continuation source, the user now sees a diagnostic message instead of a silent hang. No change for legitimate yield patterns (those with accepted spawns, delivery, async tools, or cron adds).

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — purely additive change
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No. The new test file (`sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`) is additive — it does not modify existing serialized state or snapshots, requires no migration or upgrade path.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes, for the current scope. This is a narrow additive change that fixes the UX gap (silent hang → visible diagnostic) without requiring a product decision on continuation semantics.
- **Refactor needed**: Yes — the reviewer in #100146 identified that the initial inline predicate was a fourth copy of the continuation logic that would drift. The fix extracts a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` in `incomplete-turn.ts`, reuses `hasAsyncStartedToolActivity`, and places the `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant next to its sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`. `run.ts` is now orchestration-only for this path.
- **Alternative considered**: A deeper fix at the tool level (`sessions-yield-tool.ts`) that rejects yields without continuation evidence. This would be more correct but needs a product decision on what counts as a valid continuation source, maintainer agreement on guard semantics, and plumbing of subscribe-handler state into the tool layer. Marked as future work.

### Future work (Step 2)

A follow-up PR could validate continuation sources inside `sessions_yield` tool execution and reject a yield that has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, or async work. This requires:
- Access to subscribe-handler state from the tool layer
- A product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source
- Tests for the rejection path

The diagnostic signal from this PR creates the contract surface for that future enforcement. The active-descendant check (`countActiveDescendantRuns`) already handles the most common existing-wake scenario.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: None. The change is purely additive — it only activates when `yieldDetected=true` AND payloads are empty AND no continuation evidence exists. All existing yield patterns (with spawns, delivery, async tools, cron) continue unchanged.
- **Mitigations**: The continuation check uses the same fields already tracked for `hasAttemptTerminalState`; no new state or tracing is introduced. Suppression tests (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) guard against always-false regression in the shared helper.
- **Compatibility**: Fully backward compatible. Deploying this change has no effect on sessions with legitimate yield patterns.

target.title: fix(discord): disable ws 8.21.0 receiver part limits for gateway sockets
target.body:
## Summary

ws 8.21.0 introduced `maxBufferedChunks` and `maxFragments` receiver limits (commit `[security] Limit retained message parts`) that can trigger `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and close connections with code 1008 under certain traffic patterns.

This PR explicitly sets both limits to `0` (disabled) for Discord gateway WebSocket connections, restoring the ws 8.20.0 behavior for the trusted Discord gateway peer while preserving the security fix for all other WebSocket usage.

## Changes

- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.ts`**: Base class `createWebSocket()` now passes `maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0` with a `ws.ClientOptions` cast (since `@types/ws` 8.18.1 does not yet expose these fields).
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`**: Extended `DiscordGatewayWebSocketCtor` type to include the new options; monitor gateway creation path passes the same disabled limits.
- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.test.ts`**: Added test verifying base class WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.test.ts`**: Added test verifying monitor plugin WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.proxy.test.ts`**: Updated two existing exact-match assertions to include the new options.

## Why `0` instead of raising the limits

- ws 8.21.0 treats `0` as disabled (`receiver.js:61`, `receiver.js:98`: `if (this._maxBufferedChunks > 0 && ...)`), matching the pre-8.21.0 behavior exactly.
- Discord gateway is a trusted peer; the security limits are designed to protect against untrusted senders.
- Choosing an arbitrary higher threshold would be fragile without real production traffic data to calibrate against.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: ws 8.21.0's retained-part receiver limits (`maxFragments` default 131072 / `maxBufferedChunks` default 1048576) abort a Discord gateway socket with `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` / close `1008`; this PR sets both to `0` (disabled) on the Discord gateway sockets, restoring ws 8.20.0 behavior for that trusted peer.
- **Real environment tested**: Live Discord gateway connection from a Docker `node:22-bookworm-slim` container (Node `v22.22.3`) with the repo-pinned `ws@8.21.0` installed exactly, using a real bot token (redacted), connecting to `wss://gateway.discord.gg/?v=10&encoding=json`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: build a `node:22-bookworm-slim` image with `npm install ws@8.21.0`, then run a client that constructs the gateway socket with this patch's options (`new ws.WebSocket(url, { handshakeTimeout: 30000, maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0 })`), completes the HELLO/IDENTIFY/READY handshake against the real Discord gateway, sends heartbeats, holds a 60s stable window, then closes with code 1000.
- **Evidence after fix**: Live Discord gateway run with this patch's options applied (token, `session_id`, and `resume_gateway_url` redacted):

```
[env] node=v22.22.3 ws=8.21.0
[discord] connecting wss://gateway.discord.gg (maxBufferedChunks:0, maxFragments:0)
[discord] open
[discord] HELLO heartbeat_interval=41250ms
[discord] IDENTIFY sent (token redacted)
[discord] READY received (session_id/resume_gateway_url redacted)
[discord] HEARTBEAT_ACK #1
[discord] stable window 60000ms complete
[discord] close code=1000 reason=<empty>
[result] PASS live: READY + 1 heartbeat ACK; no WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS during stable window
```

Supplemental deterministic mechanism repro against a local ws 8.21.0 gateway streaming one message in 131073 fragments (one over the client default `maxFragments`), exercising the same `ws.WebSocket` receiver path:

```
# default ws.WebSocket (ws 8.21 defaults)
[before] open
[before] error code=WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS message=Too many message fragments
[before] close code=1006 reason=<empty>

# this patch's options applied
[after] open
[after] message received: 131073 bytes - NO receiver-limit close
```

- **Observed result after fix**: On the real Discord gateway, with the disabled limits applied, the connection reaches `READY`, exchanges heartbeats, and stays connected through the 60s window with no `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and no `1008` close; the only close is the intentional client-initiated `1000`. The deterministic repro confirms the same constructor options remove the receiver-limit close that the default ws 8.21 client hits.
- **What was not tested**: the live run confirms a real gateway session stays healthy with the patched options, but does not force Discord's production fragmentation pattern on demand, does not exercise the `zlib-stream` transport, and does not drive the full OpenClaw plugin wiring end-to-end. The deterministic repro proves the ws 8.21 retained-part mechanism and that this patch's options disable the exact receiver checks, but uses a local peer rather than Discord's live framing.

## Tests

- `gateway.test.ts`: 25 passed
- `gateway-plugin.test.ts`: 17 passed  
- `provider.proxy.test.ts`: 21 passed
- TypeScript check (tsgo): clean

target.title: feat(android): tap-to-expand link previews in chat transcript
target.body:
Related: #100699

## What Problem This Solves

Bare URLs in the Android chat transcript render as plain tappable links with no way to see what's behind them before leaving the app.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds tap-to-expand link previews: a message whose text contains a safe web link shows a compact chip (domain + expand affordance) under the body; tapping it fetches OpenGraph metadata and expands into a card (title + description), and tapping the card opens the URL exactly like tapping the link. Privacy is the design driver: **no ambient fetches, ever** — network activity happens only on an explicit user tap (see #22060 for why automatic preview fetches on message content are an injection/exfiltration hazard). The preview fetch is strictly less capable than tapping the link itself: same URL, same user gesture, display-only result — fetched with a locked-down client (no cookies, no auth/proxy authenticators, no auto-redirects; each of ≤3 manual redirect hops re-validated http/https; 6s total deadline; 512KB body cap; `text/html` only). Metadata is untrusted plain text: HTML entities decoded, control characters stripped, whitespace collapsed, length-capped, rendered as plain `Text`. Results (including failures) sit in a 64-entry in-memory LRU — nothing persists to disk. The card is text-only for now: the Android transcript has no remote-image facility and this PR deliberately adds no dependency for one (og:image is parsed and safe-resolved for when one exists).

## User Impact

Android users can peek at a link's title and description before opening it, with zero background network traffic from message content. Failed lookups show a plain "No preview available" state.

## Evidence

- Focused unit suite `ChatLinkPreviewTest` green (12 tests): OG parsing (full set, `<title>` fallback, attribute-order tolerance, relative og:image resolution, control-char stripping and caps), first-URL extraction (bare URLs, markdown links, code-fence/inline-code exclusion, unsafe schemes skipped), MockWebServer fetcher (redirect chain, >3 hops rejected, non-HTML rejected, body cap, timeout), cache hit avoids refetch (request-count assertion).
- OkHttp is the app's existing HTTP client (`libs.okhttp`, used by the gateway session) — no new dependency.
- ktlint clean on changed files; `corepack pnpm native:i18n:sync` run for the new strings.
- Structured review (codex) — no actionable findings; a private-network (SSRF-style) block was consciously not added since the preview can only fetch what tapping the link already reaches, and the result never leaves the device.

target.title: fix(config): preserve empty env var values in config resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes two related issues where `resolveConfigValue` / `resolveConfigValueUncached` use `||` (boolean OR) instead of `??` (nullish coalescing), causing an explicitly-set empty environment variable to fall through to the literal config key name.

**Bug 1 — resolver fallback semantics**: When `MY_API_KEY=""`, the `||` operator treats empty string as falsy and returns the literal `"MY_API_KEY"` as the API credential. This produces a confusing "invalid API key" error from the provider instead of a clear "not configured" failure.

**Bug 2 — auth status / availability disagreement**: `ModelRegistry.getProviderAuthStatus` and `hasConfiguredAuth` disagreed about empty env-backed API keys. `getProviderAuthStatus` treated empty env vars as configured, while `hasConfiguredAuth` returned true for any provider with an `apiKey` field, so model availability, restore, and selection could still route to a provider whose status said it was unconfigured.

## Why This Change Was Made
- Replaced `||` with `??` in both `resolveConfigValue` and `resolveConfigValueUncached` so that an explicitly-set empty environment variable is preserved rather than silently reinterpreted as a literal config string.
- Updated `getProviderAuthStatus` to use `in` operator to distinguish "env var set to empty" from "env var not set", and return `configured: false` when the env var is explicitly empty.
- Updated `hasConfiguredAuth` / `getAvailable` to reject only explicitly empty env-backed `apiKey` values while preserving `AuthStorage.hasAuth` semantics (stored auth, runtime `--api-key` overrides, env-key discovery, fallback resolver) and the AWS SDK sentinel path.
- Added regression coverage for resolver, auth status, `getApiKeyAndHeaders`, availability, and runtime override paths.

## User Impact
Users who accidentally leave an API key env var set to empty will now get a consistent "API key not configured" signal across status, model availability, and runtime requests instead of a confusing "invalid API key" error from their provider. Runtime `--api-key` overrides continue to make models available.

target.title: fix(codex): resolve dynamic tool hard timeout from timeoutSeconds when timeoutMs is absent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a dynamic tool call passes `timeoutSeconds` (e.g. `{ timeoutSeconds: 120 }`) but omits `timeoutMs`, both the primary and `/btw` side-thread hard-call timeout readers only looked at `timeoutMs` and fell back to the default 90s guard. Tools that explicitly set a longer timeout in seconds (e.g. session send helpers) were capped by the default, causing premature timeouts and failed tool responses.

Fixes [#98864](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98864).

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the primary (`dynamic-tool-execution.ts`) and side-thread (`side-question.ts`) Codex dynamic-tool timeout readers read `timeoutMs` only and ignored `timeoutSeconds`. The fix applies the existing `readTimeoutSecondsAsMs` helper as a fallback when `timeoutMs` is absent or invalid — the same pattern already used for config-level image tool timeouts on both paths.

### Behavior rules

| Priority | Input | Outcome |
|----------|-------|---------|
| 1 | `timeoutMs` is valid positive number | Use `timeoutMs` (existing behavior) |
| 2 | `timeoutMs` absent/invalid, `timeoutSeconds` valid | Use `timeoutSeconds * 1000` (**new**) |
| 3 | Both absent/invalid | Fall back to configured or default timeout (existing) |

## User Impact

- **Before**: Dynamic tool call `{ timeoutSeconds: 120 }` → reads `undefined` from `timeoutMs` → falls back to 90s default → tool times out prematurely. Affected both primary and `/btw` side-thread calls.
- **After**: Dynamic tool call `{ timeoutSeconds: 120 }` → reads `120000` from `timeoutSeconds` fallback → tool gets the full 120s. Consistent across both paths.

`timeoutMs` always wins when both are present; `timeoutSeconds` is a pure fallback. No existing callers are affected.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests (58/58 passed)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(agents): add lock release timeout on attempt teardown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent run fails abnormally during tool execution (e.g., tool result lost → synthetic transcript repair → run marked as failed), the session write-lock remains held in memory beyond the run's actual lifetime.

The `disposeHeldLockAfterRetainedIdle()` path calls `waitForRetainedLockIdle()`, which blocks indefinitely when `retainedLockUseCount > 0` (a tool execution that will never complete). The `finally` block in `attempt.ts` hangs at `releaseRetainedSessionLock()`, so the lock is never released. The watchdog eventually reclaims it, but only after the full configured `maxHoldMs` (up to 17 minutes for a 15-minute agent timeout).

During this entire window, **all subsequent requests to the same session fail** with `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError` (60s acquire timeout), even though the owning run is no longer active.

### Observed behavior

```
session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=72859
```

The session remained completely unresponsive for 7+ minutes until the lock file was manually deleted. This exact scenario also hit the author's own session during development of this fix (meta-ironic proof).

## Why This Change Was Made

A single targeted fix: **add a 30-second timeout to the lock release path in the attempt finally block**.

If `releaseRetainedSessionLock()` (specifically, `waitForRetainedLockIdle()`) does not settle within 30 seconds, the finally block completes and execution continues. The lock remains in memory and is reclaimed by the existing watchdog at its configured `maxHoldMs` — no behavioral change to the watchdog itself.

Key design decisions:
- **No watchdog policy changes**: The watchdog continues to honor the configured `maxHoldMs` derived from agent timeout + grace. Compaction and long-running task windows are preserved exactly as configured.
- **Timer hygiene**: The timeout is extracted into a focused helper (`attempt.release-lock-timeout.ts`) that uses `.unref()` to avoid keeping processes alive, and `clearTimeout` in a `finally` block to prevent timer leaks on normal release.
- **Minimal blast radius**: Only the attempt teardown path is affected. Normal runs that release promptly never see the timeout.

## User Impact

Sessions recover from abnormal run failures within **30 seconds + next watchdog cycle (60s)** instead of waiting the full `maxHoldMs` (up to 17 minutes). The fix benefits any scenario where `dispose()` hangs due to stuck tool executions.

## Evidence

**Root cause trace (from real production incident):**
1. Agent run executing `exec` tool → command not found → tool result lost
2. Synthetic error result injected for transcript repair
3. Run terminates but `finally` block hangs at `releaseRetainedSessionLock()`
4. Lock still in `SESSION_LOCKS.heldEntries()` → `heldByThisProcess = true` → orphan-self-pid skipped
5. Watchdog threshold = 17 minutes → session blocked for entire duration

**Real behavior proof:**
This exact bug hit the author's own session during development of this fix. The session (`1fe741b0-c346-413e-b494-93cb26f5df22`) was locked by pid 96661 (same process, alive) for 15+ minutes across multiple attempts to interact:
```
⚠️ Agent failed before reply: session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=435021
⚠️ Agent failed before reply: session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=679231
⚠️ Agent failed before reply: session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=753583
⚠️ Agent failed before reply: session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=942030
```
The lock persisted from ~435s (7 min) through ~942s (15+ min) — consistent with a maxHoldMs of 1,020,000ms (17 min) before watchdog reclaim. With this fix, the teardown timeout would have fired at 30s, allowing the watchdog to reclaim within 1 cycle.

**Test results:**
- `attempt.release-lock-timeout.test.ts`: 4 tests passed ✅ (timer cleanup on normal release + timeout behavior)
- `session-write-lock.test.ts`: 106 tests passed ✅ (no regression to watchdog logic)
- oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors ✅

Fixes #100872

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538


### Re-verification (2026-05-20)

Local checkout at `d89f14de26`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

 ✓ cron  ../../src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (39 tests) 116ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
   Duration  152ms
```

Full cron suite (`src/cron/`) also run: 94 test files, 901 passed. The 7 failures are in unrelated files (`run-log.test.ts`, `service.failure-alert.test.ts`) pre-existing on upstream/main.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `openclaw cron run` (manual) of a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job incorrectly deletes the job. Manual runs also pollute `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `0cec2acc7a`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, counter mutations and `shouldDelete` run unconditionally — no `isManual` discriminator exists.
- **Exact steps after patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` + `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 46/46 timer regression tests pass (including 7 new #83538/#83933-specific tests). 7/7 failure-alert tests pass.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI flow; the tests exercise the same `applyJobResult` code path the Gateway calls internally.

### Key test results

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun + success | NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun + success | Deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |

## Real CLI proof at head SHA `642c3450d9` (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway built from PR head.

|------|---------|---------------|-----------------|
| A: at-job deleteAfterRun | `cron run` → `cron show` | Job deleted/disabled | `enabled: true`, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅ |
| B: every-job manual error | `cron run` → `cron show` | `nextRunAtMs` rewritten by backoff | `nextRunAtMs` unchanged ✅ |
| A+B: counters | `cron runs` | `consecutiveErrors` mutated | Unchanged ✅ |

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` no longer consumes `deleteAfterRun` one-shot jobs, and no longer perturbs retry counters, at-job retry/disable state, recurring backoff, or failure-alert cooldown.
- **Real environment tested**: Docker container built from PR HEAD `3d32c9baff`, Linux aarch64 (OrbStack), Node.js `v24.14.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`.

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: The recurring-job success/skipped branch in `applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`) recomputed `nextRunAtMs` unconditionally. This is the last unguarded schedule-mutation path in the manual-run series; guarding it completes the non-consuming manual-run invariant (#83538). This is distinct from the earlier manual-*error* backoff fix: that guarded the error branch and the backoff-recognition helpers; this guards the *success/skipped* recompute branch.
- **Real environment tested**: Local checkout at `0f2c2ef988` (rebased on `upstream/main` `0ccdef5dcf`), macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, Vitest `v4`.

The job stays enabled with counter intact.
- **Observed result after fix**: A manual ok/skipped run on a recurring job now leaves the pending scheduled backoff (or the natural next fire) untouched — the manual run is fully non-consuming across the success/skipped path as well. Disabled-job reset behavior and all non-manual scheduled behavior are unchanged.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI end-to-end for this specific success-path branch (a manual `ok` outcome requires a working LLM provider in Docker; earlier Docker CLI proofs cover the manual-run survival/backoff paths). Unit coverage exercises the exact `applyJobResult` branch the Gateway calls internally.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(skills): surface skill source shadowing
target.body:
﻿Closes #100071

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could have a workspace skill silently replace a same-named plugin, bundled, managed, or agent skill without any visible signal in skill discovery, the CLI, Control UI, or doctor lint.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the existing documented precedence behavior, but records lower-precedence same-name skill sources as shadow metadata on the active skill. The metadata is surfaced in load-time warnings, `openclaw skills list` / `openclaw skills info`, Control UI skill cards/details, and the skills-readiness doctor lint check. This intentionally does not add a fail-closed `denyShadowing` config surface because that compatibility/security policy still needs maintainer product/security direction.

## User Impact

Operators can now see when an active skill is overriding another skill source and inspect the shadowed paths before deciding whether the override is intentional. Existing intentional overrides continue to work.

## Evidence

- Current head: `7b9ad4988cd5b4528ee7b5b4132aa96f3efc7a58`.
- Claim proved: same-name lower-precedence skill sources are retained as shadow metadata and surfaced through CLI list/info and doctor lint; the current-head lint blocker is fixed.
- Changed files:
  - `src/skills/loading/workspace.ts`
  - `src/skills/discovery/status.ts`
  - `src/cli/skills-cli.format.ts`
  - `src/commands/doctor-skills-core.ts`
  - `src/flows/doctor-core-checks.ts`
  - `src/flows/doctor-core-checks.runtime.ts`
  - `ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts`
  - focused tests for the touched surfaces
- Commands / artifacts:
  - `git diff --check` -> passed.

target.title: fix(discord): messages sent during gateway reconnect are silently dropped
target.body:
Closes #56610

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord outbound messages sent while the gateway websocket was reconnecting (close codes 1005/1006 during network blips or Discord-side resets) would fail and never be delivered. The failed sends landed in the durable outbound delivery queue as pending entries, but nothing on the Discord side ever drained that queue after the gateway came back, so the messages were silently dropped from the user's perspective. WhatsApp and Telegram already drain their queued deliveries on reconnect; Discord was the gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two small, config-free changes inside the Discord plugin, mirroring the existing WhatsApp/Telegram reconnect-drain pattern:

1. `withDiscordDeliveryRetry` now treats a send failure as retryable when the account's registered gateway reports `isConnected === false`, so in-flight sends ride out short reconnect windows instead of failing immediately. The gateway is looked up with the resolved account id (the same id the lifecycle registers under, fixing the default-account lookup gap flagged on the earlier attempt in #94320), and connectivity is re-read per retry attempt so the loop stops treating errors as transport blips once the gateway is back. `DiscordError` (HTTP 4xx client errors) stays non-retryable.
2. The gateway lifecycle's status observer now fires an `onReconnect` hook on every connected transition after the initial READY, which drains pending `discord:<accountId>` queue entries via the shared `drainPendingDeliveries` SDK runtime helper. The initial connection is excluded because startup recovery already replays queued sends.

No new config surface, no protocol changes, no core changes; everything stays inside `extensions/discord` plus the existing plugin SDK seams.

## User Impact

Messages an agent sends during a Discord gateway reconnect are now delivered once the connection is re-established instead of being silently lost. Operators no longer need to restart the gateway or manually replay the delivery queue after a network blip.

## Evidence

- New unit tests:
  - `extensions/discord/src/retry.test.ts`: statusless transport errors retry while the registered gateway is disconnected; no retry when connected; `DiscordError` stays non-retryable either way; `withDiscordDeliveryRetry` end-to-end with a registered disconnected/connected gateway.
  - `extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.lifecycle.test.ts`: reconnect (websocket reopen -> READY) triggers exactly one `drainPendingDeliveries` call with `drainKey: "discord:default"` and a selector matching discord entries (including entries with an unset account id) while rejecting other channels; the initial connection triggers no drain.
- Focused run: `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/retry.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.lifecycle.test.ts` — 2 files, 48 tests passed.
- Full plugin suite: `pnpm test extensions/discord` — 163 files, 1871 tests passed.
- Typecheck: `pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- Lint/format: `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on touched files and `oxfmt --check` — clean.
- Known proof gap: no live Discord reconnect reproduction was captured for this PR (that was the blocker that stalled #94320). The reconnect-drain path is exercised by the lifecycle test at the same seam the real gateway debug/READY events flow through; happy to assist with a live repro run if maintainers want one before landing.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip heartbeat when session idle too long, back off after consecutive idle skips
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Heartbeat continues firing against a long-idle session with no user to receive output, burning expensive API tokens until the account spend cap intervenes. A heartbeat on an idle session wastes money because there's no user context to act on and no one to receive the result.

- **Problem**: `runHeartbeatOnce()` has no awareness of session staleness. It fires on a fixed interval (default 30min) regardless of whether the session has had human interaction in days or weeks. In the reported case (#98556), a single idle session consumed ~$168 in 5 days before the spend cap hit; the family chain burned ~$248 total. Even `/reset` didn't stop it — the new session inherited the same agent key and heartbeats resumed immediately.
- **Solution**: Gate the heartbeat on the resolved session's last real interaction time. If the last user/channel interaction is older than 7 days, skip the heartbeat. Additionally, track consecutive idle skips per agent and escalate to a backoff skip after 48 consecutive idle heartbeats (~1 day at 30min interval), handling edge cases like `/reset` creating fresh sessions.
- **What changed**: `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` (~40 lines of runtime logic), `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.test-utils.ts` (extended `HeartbeatSessionSeed` type), new `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.idle-gate.test.ts` (7 test cases).
- **What did NOT change**: No new config keys, types, schema, or public API. No changes to `heartbeat-wake.ts`, `heartbeat-schedule.ts`, or the scheduler layer. No behavioral change for active sessions.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #98556
- Related to #14051
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression (partial fix for the zombie-session spend scenario; #14051 remains open for the full configurable idle-timeout feature)

## Motivation

Issue #98556 reports a production incident where a `main` session idle for 21 days silently consumed ~$248 in Anthropic Opus 4.7 spend through heartbeat polls that fired every 30 minutes. The heartbeat runner had no awareness of session staleness — it checked HEARTBEAT.md content, active hours, queue busyness, and preflight conditions, but never consulted `lastInteractionAt` or any session freshness signal.

This is a runtime safety guard, not a product feature. It uses a hardcoded 7-day threshold (not a new config key) so users without any idle policy are still protected. Issue #14051 tracks the broader product decision for a configurable activity-based idle timeout; this fix provides a safety baseline until that feature lands.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Heartbeats should not fire on sessions that have been idle longer than 7 days, because there is no user to receive output and no new context for the agent to act on.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js 22, branch `fix/heartbeat-idle-gate-98556`, based on `origin/main` HEAD.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  1. Ran 7 unit tests for the idle gate + 13 existing commitment tests (zero regression).
  2. Ran a standalone proof script that calls `runHeartbeatOnce()` directly via `node --import tsx`, seeding a real session store with controlled `lastInteractionAt` values.

- **Evidence after fix**:

  ```console
  $ node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-98556-evidence/proof.mts

  === Heartbeat Idle Gate: Real Runtime Proof ===

  [1/3] Active session (1 min idle)
        status: ran

  [2/3] Idle session (8 days idle)
        status: skipped, reason: session-idle

  [3/3] Fallback (sessionStartedAt 8 days ago, no lastInteractionAt)
        status: skipped, reason: session-idle

  === All tests passed ===
  ```

  | Test case | Input | Expected | Result |
  |-----------|-------|----------|--------|
  | Active session | `lastInteractionAt = 1 min ago` | `status: "ran"` | ✅ `ran` |
  | Idle 8 days | `lastInteractionAt = 8 days ago` | `status: "skipped", reason: "session-idle"` | ✅ `skipped / session-idle` |
  | No lastInteractionAt | `sessionStartedAt = 8 days ago` | `status: "skipped", reason: "session-idle"` | ✅ `skipped / session-idle` |
  | Unit: exactly at threshold | `lastInteractionAt = 7d+1ms ago` | skip | ✅ |
  | Unit: only updatedAt | `updatedAt = 7d+1m ago` | skip | ✅ |
  | Unit: recent sessionStartedAt | `sessionStartedAt = 1 min ago` | ran | ✅ |
  | Unit: no entry | no seed data | ran (no-op) | ✅ |

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. Sessions with `lastInteractionAt` older than 7 days: heartbeat skipped with `reason: "session-idle"`.
  2. After 48 consecutive idle skips per agent: escalated to `reason: "backoff-idle"`.
  3. Sessions with recent `lastInteractionAt`: no behavioral change — heartbeat runs normally.
  4. Sessions with no `lastInteractionAt`: falls back to `sessionStartedAt`, then `updatedAt`.
  5. Sessions with no entry at all: idle gate is a no-op, execution continues to existing preflight checks.
- **What was not tested**: Live gateway soak with a real 7-day idle session (impractical in unit test); the consecutive backoff counter persistence across gateway restarts (in-memory Map, resets on restart by design).

## Root Cause

The heartbeat runner (`runHeartbeatOnce()` in `heartbeat-runner.ts:1395`) performs 13 skip checks (disabled, quiet-hours, queue busy, cron in progress, active reply runs, lane busy, pending delivery, empty HEARTBEAT.md, etc.) but never consults the resolved session's interaction staleness. The `lastInteractionAt` field has existed on `SessionEntry` since inception and is correctly preserved (not updated) by heartbeat runs — it was simply never read by the heartbeat scheduler.

This is a design omission, not a regression: the runner was built without session-activity awareness.

```
Provenance: carried forward since heartbeat runner creation — never introduced
by a specific commit, never fixed.
Confidence: clear
```

## Regression Test Plan

7 new unit tests cover the idle gate behavior. 13 existing commitment tests confirm zero regression. The change is local to `runHeartbeatOnce()` and does not touch the scheduler, wake layer, delivery path, or any public API.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with sessions idle longer than 7 days will see heartbeats automatically skipped (logged as `"session-idle"`) with no action required. Active sessions are unaffected. No new configuration or user intervention needed.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Reproduction + Verification

### Environment (unit test)
- OS: Linux x86_64
- Runtime/container: Node.js 22

### Steps (unit test)
1. Seed session store with `lastInteractionAt` set to more than 7 days ago.
2. Call `runHeartbeatOnce()` with `target: "none"`.
3. Observe `{ status: "skipped", reason: "session-idle" }`.

### Expected
Heartbeat skips on idle sessions, runs normally on active sessions.

### Actual (before fix)
Heartbeat runs regardless of session staleness.

## Evidence Checklist

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets (unit test output)
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios**: 7 test cases covering idle/active/no-entry/fallback chains; 13 existing commitment tests for regression.
- **Edge cases checked**: `lastInteractionAt` undefined, `sessionStartedAt` undefined, both undefined (only `updatedAt` available), no session entry at all.
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live gateway with real 7-day idle session (logistically impractical); the consecutive backoff counter persisting across gateway restarts (by design it's an in-memory Map).

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds a new skip path for sessions past the idle threshold; all other paths unchanged.
- [x] Config/env changes? No — no new config keys, env vars, or schema changes.
- [x] Migration needed? No.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The idle gate addresses the root cause (no staleness awareness) at the right boundary (inside `runHeartbeatOnce()`, where the session entry is already resolved and all other skip conditions are checked). The 7-day threshold is a hardcoded safety net that requires no product decision; Issue #14051 remains open for the configurable feature.
- **Refactor needed**: No.
- **Alternative considered**:
  1. Adding a new config key `heartbeat.idleTimeoutMinutes` — rejected because CLAUDE.md policy sets a high bar for new config surface, and the product decision belongs to #14051.
  2. Hooking into `evaluateSessionFreshness()` — rejected because the session's `idleMinutes` policy is about session reset, not heartbeat cost protection, and may be unconfigured.
  3. Agent-level spend circuit breaker — more comprehensive but requires cross-session accounting and new state; overkill for this fix.

## Relationship to #14051

Issue #14051 proposes a configurable activity-based heartbeat idle timeout (`heartbeat.idleTimeoutMinutes`). That feature requires a product decision (config name, schema, default behavior) and is tracked separately. This PR does **not** implement #14051. Instead, it provides a hardcoded runtime safety guard that prevents runaway cost while the #14051 product decision is pending. When #14051 is eventually implemented, its configurable threshold would naturally replace the 7-day hardcoded fallback for users who set it.

ClawSweeper's most recent review (2026-07-06) on #14051 lists "Keep existing primitives only" as an option and notes that this is a maintainer product decision; this PR's no-new-config approach aligns with the conservative end of that spectrum.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Users with legitimate heartbeat tasks that fire less often than every 7 days (e.g., a weekly heartbeat report).  
**Mitigation**: The 7-day threshold is long enough that any reasonable periodic task (daily check-in, monitoring, etc.) will fire well within the window. A weekly report would fire on day 0 (fresh session) and day 7 would be exactly at the boundary — the test covers this edge case.  
**Compatibility impact**: None for active sessions. The only sessions affected are those with no human interaction for >7 days, which are precisely the sessions that should not be heartbeating.  
**Backoff escalation risk**: The 48-consecutive-skip backoff is purely in-memory (agent-level Map) and resets on restart, so a misconfigured system can recover after a restart without operator action.

---

AI-assisted: Yes
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Human confirmed understanding of code changes: Yes

Related to #98556
Related to #14051

target.title: fix(matrix): fallback to copy+unlink on EXDEV in legacy credentials migration
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

During startup, the Matrix channel loader checks for legacy credentials and attempts to migrate them to the new paths using `fs.renameSync(legacyPath, currentPath)`.

If the legacy path and the current path lie on different mount points or filesystems (for example, when running inside containers or with different volumes), `fs.renameSync` throws an `EXDEV` error ("Cross-device link").

Since this error was caught in an empty `catch {}` block, the file was never migrated, and every future load attempt repeated the failing rename, causing repeated synchronous disk I/O failure overhead.

## Fix

Add a fallback to `fs.copyFileSync` and `fs.unlinkSync` when `fs.renameSync` fails with `EXDEV`, narrowing the caught error properly using typescript-compliant types.

## Test plan

Added a unit test `migrates legacy credentials using copy + unlink when renameSync throws EXDEV` in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/credentials.test.ts` mocking `fs.renameSync` to throw `EXDEV`. Ran tests, and all 13 tests passed.


## Evidence

Passed tests on branch `fix/1.3-exdev-matrix-credentials-migration`:
```bash
 ✓ |extension-matrix| ../../extensions/matrix/src/matrix/credentials.test.ts (13 tests)
   ✓ matrix credentials storage (13)
     ✓ migrates legacy credentials using copy + unlink when renameSync throws EXDEV
```

### Real Behavior Proof

target.title: feat(sandbox): add skipSkillsSync config option to suppress skill sync
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency.

Related: #97638

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `skipSkillsSync` as an optional boolean under `agents.defaults.sandbox` and `agents.list[].sandbox`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled:

1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace.
2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts.
3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `<location>` paths). The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides.
4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution.

## User Impact

```json5
{
  agents: { defaults: { sandbox: {
    skipSkillsSync: true,
    docker: { setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" }
  } } }
}
```

Safe-use contract: Skills must be preinstalled in the sandbox via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. The workspace bind-mount at `/workspace` shadows image-baked content, so skills baked directly at `/workspace/skills/` in a custom Docker image will not survive the mount. Use a separate path (e.g., `/preloaded-skills/`) and copy via `setupCommand`.

## Evidence

### Test coverage (7 tests pass, 0 failures)

- drops host snapshot and builds name-only prompt when `skipSkillsSync` is enabled
- drops host snapshot (no remapping) when `skipSkillsSync` is absent (regression guard)
- keeps snapshots for non-sandboxed runs (regression guard)
- eligibility preserved in sandbox prompts (regression guard)
- rebuilds sandbox prompts from materialized skill paths
- preserves remote eligibility when rebuilding sandbox prompts
- falls back to effective workspace for older sandbox contexts

### Changed files (9 files)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/types.agents-shared.ts` | Type definition |
| `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` | Zod schema with safe-use contract |
| `src/agents/sandbox/types.ts` | `SandboxWorkspaceInfo.skipSkillsSync` |
| `src/agents/sandbox/config.ts` | Config resolver propagation |
| `src/agents/sandbox/context.ts` | `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` helper + branching |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sandbox-skills.ts` | Name-only prompt when `skipSkillsSync` |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sandbox-skills.test.ts` | 2 new test cases |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` | Pass `skipSkillsSync` to sandbox context |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-system-prompt.ts` | Early return guard against host snapshot fallthrough |
